speaker: Doctor
text: I need to start by determining if these symptoms are accompanied by fever or if you have experienced any recent weight loss. Have you had a change in your bowel habits or any specific abdominal pain locations? REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count (CBC) with differential.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Complete_Blood_Count: WBC: Elevated, Hemoglobin: Slightly Decreased, Platelets: Normal

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Patient
text: I noticed swelling in my neck over the last few days. It does not hurt, but it feels enlarged and fixed. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Tuberculosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that clarification. The swelling you describe as "fixed" and non-tender is concerning; could you estimate the size of the lump and tell me if you have noticed any night sweats or unintentional weight loss recently? REQUEST TEST: Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate (ESR) and C-Reactive Protein (CRP).

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of weight loss, night sweats, and a fixed, non-tender supraclavicular lymph node despite normal inflammatory markers, I need to rule out malignancy and occult infections. Can you tell me if you have any history of alcohol use, and do you have a persistent cough or hemoptysis? REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_X-Ray and Neck_Sonography.

speaker: Patient
text: I also feel fullness in my abdomen and my clothes feel tighter. I do not have cough or recent travel.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Hodgkin Lymphoma. The combination of a fixed, non-tender supraclavicular lymph node, B-symptoms (night sweats, weight loss), and abdominal fullness despite normal inflammatory markers strongly suggests a malignant lymphoproliferative disorder, likely Hodgkin Lymphoma.
